citation: Chennoufi S, Han Y, Blanc G, De Cristofaro E, Kiennert C. PROTEAN: Federated intrusion detection in non-IID environments through prototype-based knowledge sharing. ESORICS 2025. arXiv:2507.05524

A1.evidence: 'we split the samples into 80% for training and 20% for testing' - random/stratified/temporal not stated.

A2.evidence: CNN 'consisting of two convolutional layers (64 and 128 filters)'; no windows/sequences described.

A3.evidence: No normalization/scaling/encoding described in the experimental setup.

A4.evidence: '10 rounds of federated training and three epochs of local training on each participant'.

A5.evidence: No statement that Cerberus, MOON-IDS, FedProx-IDS, FPL-IDS use the same rounds/epochs.

A6.evidence: Table 1: 'Mean and standard deviation of the macro accuracy ... averaged over three runs' reported for all baselines under the paper's alpha settings (implies authors ran them; not explicitly stated).

A7.evidence: 'we use Macro accuracy, Accuracy, F1 score, and Precision'; macro accuracy not defined as balanced accuracy; no MCC/G-mean.

A8.evidence: 'distribute the former to the participants in a non-IID manner according to the Dirichlet distribution', alpha in {0.75, 0.5, 0.25}.

A9.evidence: Table 1 mean and std over three seeds; 'we perform the Mann-Whitney U hypothesis test'.

A10.evidence: Zero-shot evaluation on unseen attack classes is within the same datasets; no held-out dataset.

notes: arXiv preprint of ESORICS 2025 paper. A7 flag for second coder: 'Macro accuracy' undefined; if it equals mean per-class recall it would be balanced accuracy. A6 rerun is inferred from baselines reported with std over seeds, not an explicit statement.
